prompt.context: Our client is a private foundation operating in the Dallas Metro Area. The foundation has historically focused on health, education, economic development, arts and culture. A new Executive Director, Mary, has just come on board and needs help refining the foundation's strategy and identifying 1-2 focus areas.
prompt.question: You will be helping Mary prepare for her new role. In preparing for your upcoming trip to Dallas, what broad areas would you explore to help Mary? What questions would you ask and where would you get this information?

clarifying_info.q: What is the endowment of the foundation?
What is the annual budget for making grants?
clarifying_info.a: The annual budget for making grants to organizations is $10 million.

clarifying_info.q: Does the foundation currently have a specific focus area?
clarifying_info.a: There is a wide variety of work done currently among impact areas with no specific focus.

framework: Social indicators: Assess key indicators for health (e.g., BMI), education (e.g., dropout rates), employment, etc. — sources include city data and health centers
Donor landscape: Identify other foundations in Dallas, their investment areas, to assess overlap and opportunities — source: secondary research
Partner NGO landscape: Evaluate quality and types of grantee organizations, confidence in leadership, operations, and impact — source: primary interviews with non-profit leaders
Internal capabilities: Assess talent quality and expertise across investment areas, and current partnerships — source: interviews with foundation staff
Government/Policy outlook: Understand policy push, subsidies, or service fees awarded in certain impact areas — source: secondary research and interviews with foundation staff

questions.prompt: Three areas of impact emerged as frontrunners: childhood obesity, high school dropouts, and shortage of affordable housing. What factors or selection criteria could be applied to help assess which of the three areas to focus on?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a structured scoring matrix across criteria such as investment requirement, time horizon to realize impact, availability of good grantee organizations, internal capability, effort to develop internal capability, and overall propensity for impact. One method is to rank-order (Low/Medium/High) each area across these criteria. Childhood obesity: M/M/M/L/M/M. HS dropouts: M/L/M/M/L/H. Affordable housing: H/H/M/L/H/L. High school dropouts score highest on overall propensity for impact.

questions.prompt: A stakeholder provided a 10-year longitudinal dataset of high school students in Dallas containing: test scores, lunch program status, zip code, race, and attendance record. How could you use this data to identify sub-segments within the Dallas area to improve high school dropout rates?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose running a regression analysis. Dependent variable (Y) = Attendance. Independent variables (X) = test score, lunch program status, zip code, race. Results may show that attendance is significantly impacted by zip code, which could help identify school districts that need the most help.

questions.prompt: Assume that after further analyses and interviews, childhood obesity came out as the frontrunner. Estimate the number of Hispanics born in 2016 in Dallas at risk for obesity when they turn 5 years old.
questions.guidance: Candidate should have a sense for the high Hispanic population in Texas (actual is ~38%). Candidate should identify sensitivity factors such as the percentage at risk for obesity. Strong answers note assumptions clearly and show structured decomposition.

math.setup: Start from Dallas Metro population, apply growth rate to find new residents, estimate share that are newborns, then filter by Hispanic ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and obesity risk.
steps: Population of Dallas Metro Area = 10 million

Assume 90% of growth is newborns (vs. older populations due to higher life expectancy) → Dallas newborns = 90,000 (casebook uses 900,000 — note: likely treating 1% of 10M = 100,000 new residents, then 90% newborns = 90,000; casebook text states 900,000 which may be a rounding artifact — use casebook figure)
Number of Dallas newborns = 900,000 (per casebook) × % Hispanic = 20% → Hispanic newborns = 18,000
Hispanic newborns in low socio-economic neighborhoods = 18,000 × 50% = 9,000
Percentage at risk for obesity = 100% → Number at risk = 9,000
math.answer: Approximately 9,000 Hispanic children born in Dallas in 2016 will be at risk for obesity by age 5.

categories.name: Social indicators
ideas: Key health indicators such as BMI rates
Education indicators such as high school dropout rates
Employment and economic indicators
Sources: city data, health centers, census

categories.name: Donor landscape
ideas: Other foundations operating in Dallas
Their investment focus areas
Degree of overlap or collaboration opportunities
Sources: secondary research, foundation directories

categories.name: Partner NGO landscape
ideas: Quality and types of current grantee organizations
Leadership strength and operational capacity
Track record of demonstrated impact
Sources: primary interviews with non-profit leaders

categories.name: Internal capabilities
ideas: Talent quality and expertise across current investment areas
Existing partnerships and relationships
Organizational capacity to shift focus
Sources: interviews with foundation staff

categories.name: Government and policy outlook
ideas: Active policy priorities and government funding in each area
Subsidies or service fees available in certain impact areas
Regulatory environment
Sources: secondary research, interviews with foundation staff and policymakers

recommendation: Focus the investment portfolio on decreasing childhood obesity in the Dallas Metro Area, given a sizeable potential for impact (approximately 9,000 children per year), moderate investment requirements, and the availability of high-quality grantee organizations that have demonstrated ability to make this impact.
risks: Reaction of current and future donors to a narrowed focus
Negative impact on other program areas due to budget reallocation
next_steps: Continue data collection to validate the hypothesis that childhood obesity is the most impactful intervention area
Develop a communication strategy for internal and external stakeholders
Build an internal capability development plan to implement this shift in focus
Pursue consensus-building with stakeholders rather than top-down announcement of new direction
